question: Why did the error rate go up on 11 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The error rate increase is not due to a sudden spike in request volume.
why_chain: The error rate increase occurred during a period of stable request volume.
The error rate increase was not preceded by a significant increase in request volume.
The error rate increase was not due to a sudden spike in request volume.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate increase was due to a sudden increase in user traffic.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate increase coincided with a stable request volume.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate increase was due to a configuration change.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate increase coincided with a deployment of a new version of the RequestHandler.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service catalog in region us-east rose from 0.31% to 1.90% (+510%), with a change point at 2026-03-11T04:00:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service catalog in region us-east: 1 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.05).
At the same time, request volume for service catalog in region us-east stayed about the same (744 per 5 min before, 831 per 5 min after, +12%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service catalog in region us-east stayed about the same (120 ms before, 120 ms after, -0%).
High error rate on catalog in us-east (catalog, us-east; 10 min after the change; record R008; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

checkout: INFO nightly backup completed (checkout, us-east; 60 min before the change; record R007; fit: describes a symptom, not a change)
